# Bound review: PR #4618

Reviewed `LLM360/comet` #4618 at `2009b20eccb5d1c6e835442f30ceb2051564b8ca`, against base `b3a331d4ea38d10987e685f4987948c21ca2cf59` and merge base `04132366986da87e4f638df94ae209375dea2259`. The branch is 12 commits behind the base; the author-intent lens is `merge-base..head`.

## Identity, scope, and requirement binding

- Canonical target: `https://github.com/LLM360/comet/pull/4618` (open, not draft).
- Reviewed scope digest: `b9058a4b1a6de71633403c307292152882caf2519b76ac52ec59072ceee6bbb2`.
- Linked requirements: `#4395`, `https://github.com/LLM360/comet/issues/4395`, digest `56983efd0193fe0dadbfd0d5c38bd4d80df79b77417d1e798cf62ad939451de9`.
- Author-intent paths (7): `docs/release/operations/command-matrix.md`, `docs/release/operations/index.md`, `mkdocs.yml`, `scripts/release/command-matrix-policy.yaml`, `scripts/validate-command-matrix.py`, `src/comet/cli/command_matrix.py`, `tests/test_command_matrix.py`.
- The PR closes #4395. The 7 acceptance criteria in the sealed issue body are the requirement source.

## Architecture decision

**Aligned.** The change follows the issue's executable convention guard design: one importable predicate module and a thin script, a reviewed policy baseline, and no CI workflow. The new module imports only core services (`comet.paths`, `comet.shared_fs`, `comet.operator_service`, `comet.error_text`, `comet.auth.keys`); it does not reverse a dependency direction. The shared-storage write uses `os.O_EXCL` claims and atomic replace, with no file lock.

The required findings below are behavior, evidence, and account-enforcement gaps. They are not unexplained boundary, dependency, or ownership violations.

## Routes

- Python deep profile: applicable (public functions, error boundaries, subprocess lifetime, test isolation).
- Documentation: applicable (`docs/release/operations/` and the operations index).
- Configuration: applicable (`scripts/release/command-matrix-policy.yaml`, `mkdocs.yml`).
- Security and shared storage: applicable (redaction, external writes, no file lock).
- CI/CD, packaging, database, generated content: N/A. No workflow, package, database, or generated artifact changed.

## Findings

### F-001 — Major — required — the user-class account check cannot fail

Location: `scripts/validate-command-matrix.py:105`.

`_account_matches` returns `account == "user"` after the admin and service branches. Root, `comet.runner`, and every member of the `comet` group therefore pass the user class. The release operator who runs the admin rows is in the `comet` group (verified on the host: `comet` members include `comet.runner` and the operator). The documented user pass is run by that operator, so the 10 user `pass` rows in the PR evidence were exercised with admin-group membership.

The docs say "The runner fails closed when the current process does not belong to that class" (`docs/release/operations/command-matrix.md:70-72`). The issue requires each row under its required account, and #4398 defines the user class as an ordinary user. A `comet` command that accidentally needs the `comet` group or root will pass this matrix. That is the exact class of failure #4387 exposed.

Closure condition: a user pass run as root, `comet.runner`, or a member of the `comet` group records `fail` (or refuses to start) with a stated reason, and a test covers the three negative cases.

### F-002 — Major — required — the record mode blocks the documented cross-account merge

Location: `src/comet/cli/command_matrix.py:652`.

`write_run_records` calls `publish_cas` without a `mode`. `publish_cas` passes `mode=None` to `_atomic_write_core_json`, which sets `0o600`. The docs tell the operator to use one `runs/command-matrix.json` for the user, admin, and service passes, and say "A later pass under another account merges by key". A 0600 file owned by the operator cannot be read by `comet.runner` when the service pass starts, and a file owned by `comet.runner` cannot be read by the operator for a later pass. `comet.paths.read_json` does not catch `PermissionError`, so the first read fails before the merge. The repository's shared cross-account records use `0o640` (for example `src/comet/load_request.py:295` and `src/comet/credential_request.py:1005`); both the operator and `comet.runner` are in the `comet` group, so a group-readable mode is available.

The manual evidence does not show a shared-file merge. The three passes can succeed only with separate record files.

Closure condition: a second account reads and merges the record written by the first account under the documented three-pass workflow, with a group-readable mode and a group-writable directory; a test or a manual receipt proves the second-account merge.

### F-003 — Major — required — the matrix never executes a command

Location: `scripts/validate-command-matrix.py:112`.

`_invocation_argv` always appends `--help`. `_run_row` runs that help invocation for every non-mutating row. `--include-mutations` only bypasses the deferral; it still runs `--help`. `--refuse` does not run the row at all: it records `exit_code=args.refusal_exit_code` and `first_line=""` from operator input (`scripts/validate-command-matrix.py:212-229`). The docs admit that the pass proves "reachability and parsing, not command behavior" (`docs/release/operations/command-matrix.md:90-92`, `189-193`).

Acceptance criterion 2 says "The matrix runs offline and reports per-command exit code and first output line". The issue's outcome says every command must work for its account class. A help exit code is zero for a command that parses but fails at runtime. The policy's `options` field is recorded but never used to build an invocation, which confirms that no real invocation exists.

Closure condition: each non-mutating row runs a reviewed real invocation offline and records its actual exit code and first output line; a failing read-only command yields `fail`; rows that cannot run offline are `deferred` or `refused_as_designed` with observed evidence; `--help` stays a parse pre-check only.

### F-004 — Minor — suggestion — the policy options are recorded but never checked

Location: `src/comet/cli/command_matrix.py:374`.

`policy_errors` builds its keys from `(binary, leaf)` only. `PolicyRow.options` is loaded but not compared, and `_render_policy` regenerates options from the derived surface rather than from the reviewed row. A removed or changed option therefore does not fail `--check`, although the docs say options are recorded "at review time" (`docs/release/operations/command-matrix.md:34`). Either compare the per-row option lists in both directions or remove the field and the claim. This is a non-blocking consistency correction.

### F-005 — Minor — suggestion — an unreadable record is replaced, not refused

Location: `src/comet/cli/command_matrix.py:635`.

`existing = read_json(path) or {}` treats an absent file and a `JSONDecodeError` file the same. `comet.paths.read_json` returns `None` for a torn or invalid document. The code then publishes a new document with only the incoming rows, so a corrupt or partially written record silently loses the prior evidence. The docs call the merge append-only. Distinguish absent from unreadable and raise `CommandMatrixError` on an unreadable existing record. This is a non-blocking evidence-integrity correction.

### F-006 — Minor — suggestion — refusal evidence can contradict the refusal

Location: `scripts/validate-command-matrix.py:212`.

`--refuse` requires `--socket-path`, but the record does not require `heartbeat_fresh` to be false or the observed exit code to be nonzero. `--refusal-exit-code` defaults to 1 but can be set to 0, and `classify_record` accepts `refused_as_designed` with exit code 0. A refusal can therefore be recorded while the offline evidence shows a live, fresh heartbeat. Require the evidence and the exit code to support the refusal, or record the observation instead of an asserted code. This is a non-blocking evidence correction.

### F-007 — Minor — suggestion — a listed command can be silently omitted from the baseline

Location: `src/comet/cli/command_matrix.py:233`.

`_walk_leaves` does `if child is None: continue` when `list_commands` returns a name but `get_command_for_context` cannot resolve it. The leaf then leaves both the derived surface and the rendered baseline, so the set-equality check passes. The issue requires that the baseline cannot silently omit a command. Raise a `CommandMatrixError` instead of skipping, and cover the case with a synthetic app. This is a non-blocking fail-closed correction.

| Implementation | 18% | 11 | Good predicates, redaction, and CAS; help-only runner, user-class fail-open, record mode, and dead options. |
| Testing and evidence | 15% | 9 | 25 behavior tests; no test of the runner, account matching, or cross-account merge. |
| Security and safety | 10% | 7 | Redaction and no-lock write are sound; user-privilege masking and the 0600 shared record weaken safety. |
| Integration and release | 7% | 4 | Documentation and no-CI are good; the documented three-account record merge is broken. |

Weighted score: **65/100 — grade D**. Verdict: **NO-GO** (three active major required findings, score below B, and an incomplete source-review coverage claim for AC2/AC3).

## Source-coverage limits

I did not run `pytest`, `ruff`, `ruff format --check`, `ty`, or `scripts/validate-command-matrix.py --check`. The source-review contract forbids using local validation as review evidence. The PR's own evidence claims 25 tests, clean ruff/format/ty, and a 173-row set-equality check. I verified the following by source inspection:

- `tests/test_command_matrix.py` has 25 `def test_` functions.
- `scripts/release/command-matrix-policy.yaml` has 173 rows: comet 23, comet-admin 124, comet-service 26; 61 `mutates: false`; all accounts are `user`/`admin`/`service`; no duplicate `(binary, leaf)` key.
- The 173 count is consistent with the issue note: at `98b3fb3b` the derivation was 172 (22/124/26); `comet version` was added in `b96a8045b` after that commit, which accounts for the extra comet row. The policy contains `comet version` as `user`, `mutates: false`.
- The changed path set is 7; no `.github` workflow and no run-record file are in it. No live production effect row is committed.
- `comet.shared_fs.claim_generation` uses `os.O_EXCL`; `publish_cas` performs a generation check; `_atomic_write_core_json` writes a temporary file and calls `replace`. No `fcntl` lock appears in the changed files or in `shared_fs.py`.
- `redact` uses `key_id_of` for a full key and `redact_credentials` for other credential shapes; `classify_record` applies it to `first_line` and `reason`. The record fields cannot carry a key by construction except `evidence`, which holds fixed socket/heartbeat fields.
- The manual pass counts match the policy distribution: user 10 pass/13 deferred, admin 44/80, service 7/19.

The PR's manual commands are elided with `...` in the body, so the exact argument vectors and environment are not reproducible from the body. The record files were written outside the repository and are not attached. I did not query CI/CD or merge readiness; those are not source-review evidence.

## Strengths

- The set-equality predicate is genuinely bidirectional, and the test file covers both directions and an uncovered leaf.
- The fail-by-default verdict table is explicit: unknown verdict, unknown account, a pass without exit 0, a refusal without an owner or reason, and a deferral without a reason all become `fail`.
- The shared-storage write follows the repository no-lock rule with an exclusive claim, a generation check, and an atomic replace.
- Redaction has separate tests for a full key identity, a labeled credential, URL userinfo, and the record fields.
- The documentation states the drift rule, the record schema, the deferral rule, the limits, and the first-live-run deferral honestly.
- The two commits are signed and carry the DCO sign-off; the history is one coherent feature change with a small reuse refactor.
